title: Understanding Urbanization
text:
Urbanization is the movement of people from rural areas into towns and cities. Tracking these changes matters because where people live affects how they work and move around, who they interact with, and the opportunities and risks they face. Governments also use this information when planning housing, transport, healthcare, and schools.

Comparing urbanization across countries is difficult because countries do not all define “urban” in the same way. A town counted as urban in one country might be classified as rural in another. When national definitions differ, international comparisons can become misleading.

One way to improve comparability is to use population and density data to classify settlements under the same rules across countries. The United Nations now uses this kind of framework in its headline urbanization figures, separating settlements into cities, towns and suburbs, and rural areas.
